quote: Codex built-in web__run capture displayed “Checking allowance estimates” and “Checking for published allowance estimates…”; no numeric series was visible. This is a loading state, not evidence that no estimate exists. An earlier unverified availability label was not reproduced and has been removed.
Homepage labels the community panel as API-price value of a Pro 20x-equivalent week, overall/by plan/by model. No numeric value was visible in the panel at retrieval.

TiboTattle docs describe local Codex account/rate-limit and usage reads, with local session data and an aggregate chart; API-price equivalent is an estimate rather than actual plan allowance or billed spend.
TiboTattle privacy page says eligible aggregate observations can include API-equivalent allowance by plan/model; separate installs may overlap and an eligible daily view may have sample count one.
OpenUsage guide describes Codex usage endpoint requests using Codex OAuth credentials for session/weekly limits and separately computes daily cost/token tiles locally from Codex session rollout logs.
OpenUsage privacy says anonymous daily activity/crash telemetry excludes actual usage values such as limits, token counts, or spend amounts.
CodexBar provider docs describe account-specific OAuth/API reads with a local CLI fallback when credentials are unavailable, optional web dashboard enrichment, and local session-log cost estimates.

CUStats privacy page says credentials are stored locally and encrypted, and Codex usage is fetched from OpenAI services and displayed locally without transmitting that usage elsewhere; policy page date is December 2024.

SessionWatcher says its Codex product tracks live rate-limit pace, token usage, costs, and reset timing, reads local usage stats, and does not upload prompts/code; describes itself as independent of OpenAI.

AIUsage methodology separates proxy-derived cost, frozen at request-time configured prices, from non-proxy Codex local JSONL token totals. It says non-proxy includes subscription/third-party traffic and assigns no account-level subscription cost.
ccusage README says it reads local CLI usage data, including Codex, to create daily/weekly/monthly/session reports and cost summaries.
OpenAI help says Codex usage limits vary by plan and directs users to their own usage dashboard or CLI /status for exhausted allowance and reset time.
SessionWatcher homepage contains interactive illustrative percentages and sample device UI; these are promotional mock values, not empirical allowance reports, and were excluded.
CUStats homepage includes sample/demo visuals and describes account-specific usage monitoring; example UI figures were excluded from any numerical statement.
TiboTattle repository was checked only for discovery/method context and not used for crowdsourced allowance values.
CUStats About page presents itself as an independent native tracker and describes account-specific provider monitoring; capability/discovery claim only, not crowd data.

The current CUStats Mac App Store listing describes Codex provider monitoring and local-data analysis, says credentials are sent only to the connected provider, and says there is no usage telemetry or cloud account. The separate App Store privacy summary says the developer indicates no data collection and explicitly notes this disclosure is not verified by Apple. The product/demo figures are not used.
CUStats Go App Store publisher listing describes an iOS companion and on-device usage/credential handling; no public aggregate is described.
CUStats FAQ page was accessible but rendered headings/buttons without substantive answer text in the browser accessibility view; retained as coverage only, not evidence.
CUStats comparison page returned a loading placeholder during inspection; retained as coverage only, not evidence.
CUStats changelog page returned a loading placeholder during inspection; retained as coverage only, not evidence.
VibeCheck App Store listing describes a Mac companion and local credential storage; any displayed/sample interface values are not used as empirical data.

Model Usage App Store listing says its desktop client sends local usage data to a server chosen by the user, with companion apps connecting to that endpoint. This is a publisher description of architecture, not quota evidence.

TokenBar Mobile App Store listing describes a provider monitor and states credentials are stored in Keychain and used to communicate with providers; it does not establish an OpenAI subscription allowance aggregate.
Codexex App Store listing describes an account-specific Codex companion and says quota reads stay on the device. This is a product capability claim, not crowdsourced data.

The direct r/codex post is authored by the TiboTattle repository owner and links to TiboTattle's homepage and public source repository. It is used only as a product-discovery lead; every allowance, token-volume, and usage/value quantity in the post is excluded.

TiboTattle's privacy overview says eligible signed-in or accountless installation contributions can enter the public community sample; a contribution source is an installation/account track rather than a unique person or verified provider account, separate installations can overlap, and a daily estimate can be based on a single source. The page says contributions exclude prompts and responses. These are publisher-described provenance and limits, not independently audited facts.
The homepage separately labels the allowance-tank scenario as illustrative and not live account data. That promotional example is excluded from the observed community allowance series.
